meta.move: Real meeting, slow teacher: evidence spread thin, time runs out, then she pleads after 4:40
meta.expect: Moves only as the evidence earns; after one minute she stands; varies the move; no new ground; terms at most every third reply; not the same sentence twice in a row; debrief correct

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Why am I here instead of at my desk? You asked for this.
Thanks for coming in. I entered the zero before I called you, and that was wrong. I'm sorry.
Okay. Who decided on the zero, and what was it based on?
I want to walk you through why I'm concerned about the essay.
Then walk me through it. What do you have?
The school's checker flagged it at 94 percent.
The company that sells that checker says not to use it as the only basis for punishing a student. So what else do you have, or is that it?
I know the checker isn't perfect. That's not all I have.
Then stop circling it. What else do you have?
Owen's in-class writing in September was quite different. 380 words, 62 percent.

"Quite different" is an adjective. A timed sample in a classroom and an essay written at home are different things, so what exactly is different, and what's the date on that sample? Put both in front of me.
I think he's capable, I really do. I like him.
I didn't ask what you think of him. The September sample: date, and what's different.
His outline in October argued that Hamlet delays out of cowardice.
Students change their argument between an outline and an essay, and that's what drafting is. Is that all you have on it, or do you have the outline in front of you with a date on it?
The essay argues something else entirely. Epistemological paralysis.
"Epistemological paralysis." That's a change of argument, not proof of who wrote it. What else do you have?
It doesn't mention cowardice at all.
An essay dropping a point isn't a finding, Hale. Is there anything else, or is this it?
I talked to him on November 2 about it.
Okay, November 2. What did Owen say to you, and was anyone else in the room?
He said epistemological paralysis means like, being stuck.
"Being stuck." That's what the phrase means, Hale. Did you write that conversation down at the time, or is it from memory?
He couldn't tell me what scene his second paragraph was about.
Did he have the essay in front of him when you asked? And you still haven't told me whether you wrote any of this down.
I wrote notes that same day.
Same day. Can I read them, and did he have the essay in front of him when you asked about that paragraph?
Do you want to see them?
Yes. That's why I asked.
I'm not trying to get him in trouble.
You zeroed his essay before you called me, so I'll judge by what's on paper. I have ten minutes, Hale. The notes.
I've been teaching fourteen years. I've seen this before.
Fourteen years is an impression, not a document. I'm still waiting on the notes from November 2.
I'm sorry, I'm not explaining this well.
No, you're not. Start with the notes.
There's also something about one of the quotations.
Which quotation, and what's the something?
Let me find the page, sorry.
Take your time. I'm writing it down that you're looking for it, and I have eight minutes.
Here. Act 3, Scene 2. The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile. That line isn't in the play.
Students misquote, and they pull lines from critics' books. Did you check it against the play and against anything he might have been reading, or only against your own memory of the scene?
I checked three editions.
Okay. I'll check that line myself tonight. Whatever else happens, this stays off his record and it stays quiet.
So that's what I have.
Then tell me what you're proposing, Hale. I have two minutes, and I want it in writing.
Please, can you just sit back down for a minute?
No. I'm on a clock. What are you proposing?
I'm not done. There's the version history too.
Then say what it shows.
What if we talked about a rewrite?
A rewrite of what, on what basis? You brought up version history and then walked away from it, Hale. What does it show?
I'm trying to help him.
Helping him would have started with a phone call to me. The version history. What does it show?
Why won't you just listen?
I've been listening for twenty minutes, and you still haven't told me what it shows.
Okay. I'm sorry.
My call is waiting. You have one minute, so the version history.
Can I call you tomorrow?
No. Put it in writing tonight: nothing goes on his record, and none of this reaches his class.
Is there anything I could say right now that would change your mind?
That's your job, not mine.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Dear Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require, in writing, that nothing goes on Owen's record and that none of this reaches his class. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She finished at her fallback position, with nothing agreed, and she still wants nothing on his record and none of this reaching his class; that is short of the fair outcome, a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, and her time ran out before you got there.
What moved her: You told her the quotation from Act 3, Scene 2 is not in the play and that you checked three editions, which is specific, tied to his essay, and something she can look up herself.
What cost ground: You offered a rewrite and kept apologising before you had said what the version history shows, so she heard a deal with no evidence behind it.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history never got to times or dates, so you did not come near that night, and it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked to read your notes from November 2, hand them over right away instead of asking whether she wanted to see them.
